overlap_rationale: Both full texts report sequential, nested stages of the same Verbal Autopsy with Participatory Action Research (VAPAR) cycle on lack of safe water in the Agincourt Health and Socio-Demographic Surveillance System (HDSS), Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Mpumalanga, South Africa. Study B (Hove et al., 2019) reports Stage 1 alone: 8 weekly community PAR and Photovoice workshops (June–September 2017) with 16 community stakeholders in the village that nominated clean water (8 initial participants plus 8 newly recruited women of reproductive age, within a 3-village cohort of 48 community participants). Study A (Hove et al., 2021) reports the full multi-stage process: it explicitly incorporates Stage 1 (tabulating the 8 community workshops with N=52 including 4 researchers in Table 1, citing Study B as reference [37] as the prior publication of Stage 1 results, and summarizing those Stage 1 community findings alongside 2014/15 Agincourt VA mortality data in its Results), and then extends the empirical data to 3 multisectoral analysis workshops in January–March 2018 (n=18, 17, 18) and 2 district-level action-planning workshops in September–October 2018 (n=19, 20) involving provincial/district government departments, NGOs, researchers, and a subset of the Stage 1 community stakeholders. Because Study B's sample and qualitative outputs form Stage 1 of Study A while Study A adds five 2018 multisectoral workshops with additional government/NGO actors, there is partial sample and data overlap.
study_a_sample_and_data: Agincourt HDSS, Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Mpumalanga, South Africa (VAPAR programme). Three-stage qualitative PAR design: Stage 1 (June–September 2017, 8 community workshops with 16 community co-researchers in the water-nominating village / 48 community participants + 4 researchers = 52 across 3 villages, combined with 2014/15 Agincourt VA mortality data); Stage 2 (January–March 2018, 3 multisectoral analysis workshops in Mbombela/Agincourt with n=18, 17, and 18 community, MDoH, other provincial/district government, and researcher participants); and Stage 3 (September–October 2018, 2 local action-planning workshops at Agincourt HDSS offices with n=19 and 20 community, government, water agency, NGO, and researcher stakeholders).
study_b_sample_and_data: Agincourt HDSS, Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Mpumalanga, South Africa (VAPAR programme). Stage 1 community PAR and Photovoice study (8 weekly consensus-building workshops; dates reported in Study A as June–September 2017) across 3 villages (24 initial + 24 newly recruited = 48 community participants aged >=18), focusing on the 1 village ('Village A') that nominated lack of clean, safe water (n=8 original community stakeholders + n=8 newly recruited women of reproductive age = 16 community co-researchers).
